definition: An ordered list of numbers, called terms; $u_{n}$ is the $n$th term itself, not the sum of the terms up to it.
A sequence in which each term is the previous term plus the same constant $d$, which may be negative, so the terms rise or fall by equal steps.

In an arithmetic sequence, the constant $d = u_{n+1} - u_{n}$, the same for every pair of consecutive terms and negative when the terms fall; for real data that is only roughly arithmetic it can only be estimated.
The sum of the terms of a sequence; $S_{n}$ is the sum of the first $n$ terms, not the $n$th term.
A short way to write a sum: $\sum_{r=a}^{b} f(r)$ means put every whole number $r$ from $a$ to $b$, both included, into $f(r)$ and add the results.
Interest worked out each period on the original amount only, so the same sum is added every period and the balances form an arithmetic sequence rather than a geometric one.
